topics.title: Introduction: corpuscular and wave models of light

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the predictions of the corpuscular and wave models of light for refraction and identify which experiment settled the question.
Explain how Maxwell's electromagnetic theory resolved the difficulty of light travelling through vacuum.
Define a wavefront and identify spherical and plane wavefronts and their relation to rays.
Use Huygens' construction of secondary wavelets to find the position of a wavefront at a later time.

topics.title: Refraction and reflection of plane waves using Huygens principle

concepts.learning_objective: Derive Snell's law and the law of reflection using Huygens' construction.
Explain why frequency stays constant while speed and wavelength change on refraction.
Describe how wavefronts change on passing through prisms and lenses and on reflection from mirrors.

topics.title: Coherent and incoherent addition of waves

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish coherent and incoherent sources and the resulting intensity patterns.
State the path and phase difference conditions for constructive and destructive interference.
Apply I = 4 I0 cos^2(phi/2) to find the intensity at a point in an interference pattern.

topics.title: Interference of light waves and Young's experiment

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Young's arrangement produces two coherent sources from a single source.
Calculate positions of bright and dark fringes and the fringe width in Young's double-slit experiment.
Describe the single-slit diffraction pattern and locate its minima at angles n(lambda)/a.
Compare interference and diffraction and relate the double-slit pattern to both.
Explain polarisation as a property of transverse waves and describe linearly polarised and unpolarised light.
Apply Malus' law to find the intensity of light transmitted through combinations of polaroids.
